ActorTalk: Appearance: A low-poly, topological piece shaped as a "half-corrupted homeworld." One side is a shattered mass in cold grays, warped by the Punishing and jagged like apocalyptic ruins. The other side forms a powerful female silhouette. Even with parts missing, she reaches forward, her fingertips aimed straight at the "future" and "hope."
Sharp lines cut like shattered blades. The gray metallic surface catches fractured light, conveying the tension of charging toward hope while trapped in darkness.
Type: A counterattack-themed topological sculpture, blending digital art with physical form, created jointly by WGAA and historians.
Meaning: This work stands as a symbol of the Reconquista Age's spirit in the Olympia Art Gallery.

The artists focus on Earth's refusal to give in under the Punishing onslaught. Through broken, geometric forms, the piece depicts both the sacrifice and the glory of the Reconquista Age: One half bears the scars of a wounded planet, while the outstretched form represents warriors answering the call and pushing toward hope.
Its shifting colors represent Earth's scars intertwined with humanity's will to fight back—an unextinguished ember beneath steel skies, sworn to reclaim our homeworld.
